plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in the last weeks of winter. It is widely cultivated in East Asia for ornament and for its sour fruit, which is pickled or made into liqueur.
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as symbols of perseverance because they bloom in cold weather, and in Japan ume viewing traditionally precedes cherry blossom viewing.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and naturalizes in woodlands, churchyards and gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galanthamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden flower balls. It is a vital source of pollen for native insects and birds and grows in woodland and scrub.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July–October in Australia, with some flowering earlier in mild areas)
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with giant flower heads made of pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It thrives in the fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor, well-drained soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn peak, with flowers present through much of the year (February in the Southern Hemisphere is within the season)
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its fire-adapted structure lets the plant survive the regular wildfires of the fynbos.
